sections.heading: Why Tempered Glass Matters for Your Property
sections.body: Tempered glass is manufactured through a controlled heating and rapid cooling process that makes it significantly stronger than standard annealed glass. When it does break, it shatters into small, rounded fragments rather than sharp shards, which greatly reduces the risk of serious injury. This makes it the preferred choice for doors, sidelites, shower enclosures, storefronts, and any glazed opening where human impact is a concern. For commercial properties in Chantilly — including office parks, retail centers, and mixed-use developments — tempered glass is commonly specified in entrances and curtainwall systems. For residential clients, it appears in patio doors, large windows, and bathroom glass. Understanding what tempered glass does and why it is used helps property owners make informed decisions when replacement becomes necessary. Our team can assess your existing glazing, confirm what type of glass is in place, and recommend the appropriate replacement to restore safety and function to your space.

sections.heading: What to Expect During the Replacement Process
sections.body: The tempered glass replacement process begins with a thorough assessment of the damaged glazing. Our technicians identify the glass type, thickness, size, and any special characteristics such as tinting, low-e coatings, or insulated glass unit construction. Tempered glass cannot be cut or modified after tempering, so every replacement piece must be ordered to precise dimensions from a fabricator. Once the glass is ready, our crew removes the broken material safely, cleans the frame, inspects the glazing channel and hardware, and installs the new tempered lite with appropriate setting blocks and glazing tape or compound. For insulated glass units, we replace the full sealed unit to maintain thermal performance. The finished installation is inspected for proper fit, secure retention, and clean appearance before we consider the job complete. We communicate clearly throughout the process so property managers and homeowners are never left wondering about status or timing.

faq.q: How long does tempered glass replacement typically take?
faq.a: The timeline depends on the size and specifications of the glass needed. Standard tempered glass for common door and window sizes can often be sourced and installed within one to two business days. Custom sizes or specialty glass may require additional fabrication time. We provide honest lead time estimates upfront so you can plan accordingly.

faq.q: Can tempered glass be repaired, or does it always need to be replaced?
faq.a: Tempered glass cannot be repaired once it is cracked or broken. Unlike laminated glass, tempered glass is under internal stress from the manufacturing process, and any crack typically causes it to shatter into its characteristic small fragments. Full replacement is the only safe and effective solution when tempered glass is damaged.
